criteria.name: Major
criteria.description: Agent A makes a claim “c” to Agent B

criteria.name: Minor 1
criteria.description: Claim “c” is vague or ambiguous in a way that permits multiple interpretations

criteria.name: Minor 2
criteria.description: Ambiguity benefits A by allowing denial, reinterpretation, or opportunistic use of “c”

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.description: Claim “c” should be scrutinised for intentional ambiguity

criteria.name: CQ1
criteria.description: Which terms, phrases, or pieces of information in “c” are ambiguous?

criteria.name: CQ2
criteria.description: How do possible interpretations affect B's beliefs or actions?

criteria.name: CQ3
criteria.description: Does A have a record of making and exploiting ambiguous statements?

criteria.name: CQ4
criteria.description: What benefit does A gain from keeping “c” vague?

criteria.name: CQ5
criteria.description: Would clarification of “c” change B's interpretation?
